name: Gynecomastia compression vest

lead: A gynecomastia compression vest is an elastic undershirt that flattens the chest so enlarged male breast tissue shows less through clothing. It does not change the tissue underneath.
Gynecomastia is common in adolescence, and most teenage cases resolve within about two years. No studies were found that test compression garments for it.

paras: Pressure from the elastic fabric holds the chest tissue flatter against the body, which changes the outline under a shirt.

No published safety data for these vests were found. Medical sources describe observation, medication and surgery as the management routes for persistent gynecomastia, and note that some causes, such as drugs or illness, are evaluated by clinicians.

lead: A gynecomastia compression vest is a tight-fitting undershirt or vest, sold mainly to men, that presses the chest flat so that enlarged male breast tissue is less visible under clothing. It conceals rather than treats the condition. Gynecomastia is the benign enlargement of one or both male breasts caused by an imbalance between estrogens and androgens. [1]

No published studies were found that test compression garments for gynecomastia. Medical sources describe observation, medication and surgery as the management routes, and the Wikipedia article on the condition does not mention compression garments. [1]
infobox: Gynecomastia: affects up to 70 percent of adolescent boys to some degree [1]

paras: Wikipedia reports that about 35 percent of men are affected at some point, and that up to 70 percent of adolescent boys develop it to some degree, typically peaking at ages 13 to 14. About 75 percent of adolescent cases resolve within two years without treatment. [1]

Listed causes include puberty, ageing, obesity, certain medications and substances such as anabolic steroids and spironolactone, chronic illness and hypogonadism, and the cause is unknown in about a quarter of cases. [1] Treatment is generally considered when it persists beyond two years or causes pain or embarrassment; options include stopping an offending drug, tamoxifen and other medications, and surgery such as liposuction-assisted mastectomy. [1]

Vests are elastic compression garments worn against the skin that flatten the chest. They are marketed as a way to hide gynecomastia, including for people who are waiting for puberty-related cases to resolve or who are considering surgery. This description reflects how such products are generally sold; no source examined for this entry reviews them.

No studies found. Research on compression vests in other settings covers different conditions, such as a pilot study of a compression vest for breast and chest-wall edema in women treated for breast cancer, which reported on pain symptoms, and trials of pocket compression devices after cardiac device implantation. These studies do not address gynecomastia. [2][3]
